title: A sharp fs monoid is the lattice part of its rational cone
statement: Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid, written additively [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and assume $P$ is sharp: $0$ is its only invertible element. Let $G=P^{\rm gp}$, put $V=G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, and let $C\subseteq V$ be the rational cone generated by the image of $P$, namely the set of finite sums $\sum_i q_i(p_i\otimes1)$ with $q_i\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}$ and $p_i\in P$. Then: (a) $G$ is a free abelian group of finite rank, that is, it has a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis, so that $g\mapsto g\otimes1$ embeds $G$ in $V$; (b) $C$ is a pointed rational polyhedral cone spanning $V$, meaning that there are finitely many $v_1,\ldots,v_m\in G$ with $C=\{\sum_j q_jv_j:q_j\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}\}$, that $C\cap(-C)=\{0\}$, and that every element of $V$ is a difference of two elements of $C$; (c) $P=C\cap G$ inside $V$. The case $P=\{0\}$, $G=0$, $V=0$, $C=\{0\}$ is included.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.17, printed p. 101 (saturation), and Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103 (rational polyhedral fan description); the lattice-cone formulation is expanded here. Kato 1994, Toric singularities, is WANTED for the underlying toric monoid argument.

proof.text: Identify $P$ with its image in $G$ using integrality in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Choose finite monoid generators $p_1,\ldots,p_m$. By the presentation of group completion in that node, every $g\in G$ is an integer combination of the $p_j$, hence a difference $a-b$ with $a,b\in P$. Thus $G$ is finitely generated. If $ng=0$ for an integer $n>0$, both $ng$ and $n(-g)$ lie in $P$. Saturation puts both $g$ and $-g$ in $P$. Their sum is zero in $G$; injectivity of $P\to G$ makes their sum zero in $P$. Thus they are additive inverses in $P$, so sharpness gives $g=0$. Consequently $G$ is torsion-free.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] to the finitely generated torsion-free abelian group $G$ established in Step 1. It gives $r\in\mathbf N$ and a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$: every $g$ is uniquely $\sum_k n_ke_k$ with $n_k\in\mathbf Z$. This proves the finite-free assertion in (a).

source.place: Expose VI 3.7(a), printed p. 75, finite torsion-free group completion; the finite-basis result is the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Write $i(g)=g\otimes1$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-monoid-rational-coordinates] to the basis from Step 2 and generators $p_j$ from Step 1: their nonnegative integral sums are exactly the image of $P$ in $G$. Its coordinate formula gives $L_k(g\otimes1)=\lambda_k(g)$, so $g\otimes1=0$ forces every integral coordinate to vanish and $g=0$, proving (a). Its cone equality gives finite lattice generators for $C$. Choose integers $b_{kj}$ expressing each $e_k$ in the $p_j$. For $x\in V$, put $c_j=\sum_k L_k(x)b_{kj}$. Its signed formula gives $x=u-v$, with $u=\sum_j\max(c_j,0)i(p_j)$ and $v=\sum_j\max(-c_j,0)i(p_j)$. Both lie in $C$ since their coefficients are nonnegative. This proves finite generation and spanning in (b).

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-rational-cone-simultaneous-lifts] with the injection $i(g)=g\otimes1$ just proved and the image submonoid $P\subseteq G$, which contains $0$ and is closed under addition. It identifies $i(g)\in C$ with $ng\in P$ for some $n\ge1$. Saturation in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] then gives $g\in P$. Conversely $i(p)\in C$ for $p\in P$ by its one-term expression. Thus $P=C\cap G$, proving (c).

proof.text: For $x,-x\in C$, [lem-trf-rational-cone-simultaneous-lifts] supplies $N\ge1$ and $a,b\in P$ with $i(a)=Nx$, $i(b)=-Nx$ and $a+b=0$ in $G$. The injective map $P\to G$ from [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] therefore gives $a+b=0$ in $P$. Thus $b$ is an additive inverse of $a$ in $P$, and sharpness gives $a=0$. Then $Nx=0$; division by the nonzero rational $N$ gives $x=0$. The empty sum gives $0\in C$, proving pointedness and completing (b). For $P=\{0\}$, its group completion is zero, the empty-basis case of the coordinate lemma gives $V=0$, and the defining sums give $C=\{0\}$.
